title.zh: 卷三五 補列傳第二七 裴讓之 弟諏之 讞之 李構 張宴之 陸卬 王松年 劉禕
title.en: Volume 35 Biographies 27: Pei Rangzhi; Li Guo; Zhang Yanzhi; Lu Ang; Wang Songnian; Liu Yi
title.raw: 卷三五 補列傳第二七 裴讓之 弟諏之 讞之 李構 張宴之 陸卬 王松年 劉禕 Volume 35 Biographies 27: Pei Rangzhi; Li Guo; Zhang Yanzhi; Lu Ang; Wang Songnian; Liu Yi

sentences.zh: 裴讓之 弟諏之 讞之 皇甫和 李構 張宴之 陸卬 王松年 劉禕

translations.literal: Pei Rangzhi; younger brothers Souzhi and Yanzhi; Huangfu He; Li Gou; Zhang Yanzhi; Lu Ang; Wang Songnian; Liu Yi
translations.idiomatic: Pei Rangzhi; younger brothers Souzhi and Yanzhi; Huangfu He; Li Gou; Zhang Yanzhi; Lu Ang; Wang Songnian; Liu Yi

sentences.zh: 裴讓之，字士禮。

translations.literal: Pei Rangzhi, styled Shili.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Rangzhi, styled Shili.

sentences.zh: 年十六喪父，殆不勝哀，其母辛氏泣撫之曰：「棄我滅性，得為孝子乎？

translations.literal: At age sixteen he lost his father, grief nearly beyond bearing; his mother the Lady Xin wept as she comforted him, saying, "Would you abandon me and destroy your nature—could that make you a filial son?
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he lost his father, grief nearly more than he could bear; his mother Lady Xin wept as she comforted him, saying, "Would you abandon me and destroy yourself—could that make you a filial son?

sentences.zh: 」由是自勉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he urged himself on.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he forced himself to recover.

sentences.zh: 辛氏高明婦則，又閑禮度。

translations.literal: Lady Xin was a lofty and clear exemplar among women, and also versed in ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xin was an exemplary woman of high principle and also well versed in ritual.

sentences.zh: 夫喪，諸子多幼弱，廣延師友，或親自教授。

translations.literal: When her husband died, the sons were mostly young and weak; she widely invited teachers and friends, or personally instructed them.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband's death the sons were still young; she brought in many tutors or taught them herself.

sentences.zh: 內外親屬有吉凶禮制，多取則焉。

translations.literal: Kin within and without, for auspicious or inauspicious occasions and ritual rules, mostly took her as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives near and far took her as their model for ritual on happy and mournful occasions.

sentences.zh: 讓之少好學，有文俊辯，早得聲譽。

translations.literal: Rangzhi from youth loved learning, had literary talent, sharp eloquence, and early won reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Rangzhi loved learning from youth; gifted in letters and sharp in debate, he won an early reputation.

sentences.zh: 魏天平中舉秀才，對策高第。

translations.literal: In Wei times under Tianping he was recommended as xiucai; in policy responses he ranked at the top.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei in the Tianping era he was recommended as xiucai and ranked first in the policy examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷屯田主客郎中，省中語曰：「能賦詩，裴讓之。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to Director of Agriculture and Master of Guests in the Masters of Writing; within the ministry they said, "Who can compose poetry? Pei Rangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of agriculture and master of guests in the masters of writing; at court they said, "Who can write poetry? Pei Rangzhi.

sentences.zh: 」為太原公開府記室。

translations.literal: " He served as recorder for the Prince of Taiyuan's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: " He became recorder on the staff of the Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 與楊愔友善，相遇則清談竟日。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Yang Yin; when they met they held pure talk the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Yang Yin; whenever they met they talked the day away.

sentences.zh: 愔每云：「此人風流警拔，裴文季為不亡矣。

translations.literal: Yin would often say, "This man's spirit is alert and outstanding—Pei Wenji is not dead after all.
translations.idiomatic: Yin often said, "This man's spirit is striking and outstanding—Pei Wenji lives on in him.

sentences.zh: 」梁使至，帝令讓之攝主客郎。

translations.literal: " When a Liang envoy arrived, the emperor had Rangzhi act as master of guests attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " When a Liang envoy arrived, the emperor had Rangzhi serve as acting master of guests.

sentences.zh: 第二弟諏之奔關右，兄弟五人皆拘繫。

translations.literal: His second younger brother Souzhi fled to Guanxi; all five brothers were detained.
translations.idiomatic: His second brother Souzhi fled to the western passes; all five brothers were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 神武問曰：「諏之何在？

translations.literal: Gao Huan asked, "Where is Souzhi?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan asked, "Where is Souzhi?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「昔吳、蜀二國，諸葛兄弟各得遂心，況讓之老母在，君臣分定，失忠與孝，愚夫不為。

translations.literal: " He answered, "In former times Wu and Shu were two states, yet the Zhuge brothers each had his wish fulfilled; how much more when Rangzhi's old mother is here—ruler and minister roles are fixed; to lose both loyalty and filial piety is what a fool would not do.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Long ago Wu and Shu were two realms, yet the Zhuge brothers each got his way; all the more when Rangzhi's aged mother is here—lord and subject each have his place; to lose loyalty and filial piety together is what no fool would choose.

sentences.zh: 伏願明公以誠信待物，若以不信處物，物亦安能自信？

translations.literal: I humbly wish the lord will treat things with sincerity and trust; if you treat things without trust, how can things in turn trust you?
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, my lord, to meet the world with sincerity; if you meet the world without trust, how can the world trust you in return?

sentences.zh: 以此定霸，猶卻行而求道耳。

translations.literal: To settle hegemony on this basis is like walking backward to seek the Way.
translations.idiomatic: To found dominion on that is like walking backward to find the road.

sentences.zh: 」神武善其言，兄弟俱釋。

translations.literal: " Gao Huan approved his words, and the brothers were all released.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan approved his reply, and the brothers were all freed.

sentences.zh: 歷文襄大將軍主簿，兼中書舍人，後兼散騎常侍，聘梁。

translations.literal: He served successively as chief clerk to Gao Cheng as grand general, concurrently secretariat attendant, later concurrently regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and as envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk on Gao Cheng's staff as grand general, then as concurrent secretariat attendant and later as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry on a mission to Liang.

sentences.zh: 文襄嘗入朝，讓之導引，容儀蘊藉，文襄目之曰：「士禮佳舍人。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng once entered court; Rangzhi guided him in; his bearing was composed and refined; Gao Cheng looked at him and said, "Shili is a fine attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Gao Cheng went to court Rangzhi led him in with composed, refined bearing; Gao Cheng glanced at him and said, "Shili is a fine gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 」遷長兼中書侍郎，領舍人。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to senior concurrent secretariat vice director, still holding attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to senior concurrent secretariat vice director while retaining his attendant post.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，靜帝遜居別宮，與諸臣別，讓之流涕歔欷。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, Emperor Jing withdrew to a separate palace to take leave of the ministers; Rangzhi wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, Emperor Jing retired to a side palace to bid the ministers farewell; Rangzhi wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 以參掌儀注，封寧都縣男。

translations.literal: For helping manage ritual regulations he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: For helping draft ritual regulations he was enfeoffed as baron of Ningdu county.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以為黃門郎，或言其體重，不堪趨侍，乃除清河太守。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make him yellow gate attendant; some said his body was too heavy and he could not bear hurrying in attendance, so he was instead made grand administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint him yellow gate attendant, but some said he was too heavyset for palace attendance, so he was made grand administrator of Qinghe instead.

sentences.zh: 至郡未幾，楊愔謂讓之諸弟曰：「我與賢兄交款，企聞善政。

translations.literal: Not long after he reached the commandery, Yang Yin said to Rangzhi's younger brothers, "Your worthy elder brother and I are close in friendship; I look forward to hearing of good government.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he took office in the commandery, Yang Yin told Rangzhi's brothers, "Your elder brother and I are close; I have been eager to hear of his good rule.

sentences.zh: 適有人從清河來，云姦吏斂跡，盜賊清靖。

translations.literal: Just now someone came from Qinghe and said corrupt clerks have drawn in their claws and bandits are quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Someone has just arrived from Qinghe saying corrupt officials have pulled back and robbers are subdued.

sentences.zh: 期月之期，翻然更速。

translations.literal: The target of a full month has been overturned still faster.
translations.idiomatic: What should have taken a month has come about even sooner.

sentences.zh: 」清河有二豪吏田轉貴、孫舍興久吏姦猾，多有侵削，因事遂脅人取財。

translations.literal: " In Qinghe were two powerful clerks, Tian Zhuangui and Sun Shexing—long-serving, crafty and slippery, who often shaved off shares and, using incidents, then extorted people's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: " Qinghe had two powerful clerks, Tian Zhuanggui and Sun Shexing—veteran, cunning officials who often skimmed funds and used any pretext to extort money.

sentences.zh: 計贓依律不至死。

translations.literal: Calculating the booty by law did not reach death.
translations.idiomatic: By law the amount of stolen goods did not warrant death.

sentences.zh: 讓之以其亂法，殺之。

translations.literal: Rangzhi, because they had disrupted the law, killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Rangzhi executed them for subverting the law.

sentences.zh: 時清河王岳為司州牧，遣部從事案之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Yue of Qinghe was inspector of Si province; he sent a bureau aide to investigate the case.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Yue of Qinghe was governor of Si province and sent a staff investigator to review the case.

sentences.zh: 侍中高德政舊與讓之不協，案奏言：「當陛下受禪之時，讓之眷戀魏朝，嗚咽流涕，比為內官，情非所願。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Gao Dezheng had long been at odds with Rangzhi; in the memorial of investigation he said, "When Your Majesty received the mandate, Rangzhi cherished the Wei court, sobbed and wept; compared with being an inner-court official, his heart was not in it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Gao Dezheng had long disliked Rangzhi; in his report he wrote, "When Your Majesty took the throne, Rangzhi clung to the Wei house and wept; service at court was not what he wished.

sentences.zh: 」旣而楊愔請救之，云：「罪不合死。

translations.literal: " Before long Yang Yin pleaded for his life, saying, "The crime does not merit death.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Yin then pleaded for him, saying, "The offense does not deserve death.

sentences.zh: 」文宣大怒，謂愔曰：「欲得與裴讓之同冢耶！

translations.literal: " Gao Yang was greatly enraged and said to Yin, "Do you wish to share a tomb with Pei Rangzhi?
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Yang flew into a rage and said to Yin, "Do you want to lie in the same grave as Pei Rangzhi?

sentences.zh: 」於是無敢言者。

translations.literal: " Thereupon none dared speak further.
translations.idiomatic: " After that no one dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 事奏，竟賜死於家。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, in the end he was ordered to die at home.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was finalized, he was ordered to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 讓之次弟諏之。

translations.literal: Rangzhi's next younger brother was Souzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Rangzhi's next younger brother was Souzhi.

sentences.zh: 諏之，字士正，少好儒學，釋褐太學博士。

translations.literal: Souzhi, styled Shizheng, from youth loved Confucian learning; on leaving the robe he became erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Souzhi, styled Shizheng, loved Confucian studies from youth and on first office became an erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 嘗從常景借書百卷，十許日便返。

translations.literal: He once borrowed a hundred scrolls from Chang Jing and returned them in some ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Once he borrowed a hundred scrolls from Chang Jing and returned them in about ten days.

sentences.zh: 景疑其不能讀，每卷策問，應答無遺。

translations.literal: Jing suspected he had not read them; he questioned him on each scroll, and he answered without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Jing doubted he could have read them and quizzed him scroll by scroll; he answered without a gap.

sentences.zh: 景嘆曰：「應奉五行俱下，禰衡一覽便記，今復見之於裴生矣。

translations.literal: Jing sighed and said, "Ying Feng could take in the Five Classics at once, Mi Heng remembered on a single reading—today I see it again in Master Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sighed, "Ying Feng took in the Five Classics at a stroke and Mi Heng remembered at one glance—today the same gift appears in Master Pei.

sentences.zh: 」楊愔闔門改葬，托諏之頓作十餘墓誌，文皆可觀。

translations.literal: " When Yang Yin had his whole clan reburied, he entrusted Souzhi to dash off more than ten epitaphs at once; the texts were all worth reading.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yang Yin reburied his entire clan, he had Souzhi write more than ten epitaphs in quick succession, each of them presentable.

sentences.zh: 讓之、諏之及皇甫和弟亮並知名於洛下，時人語曰：「諏勝於讓，和不如亮。

translations.literal: Rangzhi, Souzhi, and Huangfu He's younger brother Liang were all famed in Luoyang; people of the time said, "Souzhi surpasses Rangzhi; He is not the equal of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Rangzhi, Souzhi, and Huangfu He's brother Liang were all famous in Luoyang; contemporaries said, "Souzhi outdoes Rangzhi; He cannot match Liang.

sentences.zh: 」司空高乾致書曰：「相屈為戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: " Minister of Works Gao Gan sent a letter saying, "I would bend you to serve as household census aide.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of works Gao Gan wrote inviting him to serve as household census aide.

sentences.zh: 」諏之復書不受署。

translations.literal: " Souzhi replied by letter and would not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " Souzhi answered by letter and declined the post.

sentences.zh: 沛王開大司馬府，辟為記室。

translations.literal: When Prince Kai of Pei opened his grand marshal's office, Souzhi was summoned as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kai of Pei opened his grand marshal's office, Souzhi was recruited as recorder.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴後，諏之留在河南，西魏領軍獨孤信入據金墉，以諏之為開府屬，號曰「洛陽遺彥。

translations.literal: After the move to Ye, Souzhi remained in Henan; Western Wei commanding general Dugu Xin entered and seized Jinyong, made Souzhi staff officer of his office, and styled him "the surviving worthy of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved to Ye, Souzhi stayed in Henan; Western Wei's commanding general Dugu Xin seized Jinyong, appointed Souzhi to his staff, and called him "the last eminent man of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 」信敗，諏之居南山，洛州刺史王元軌召為中從事。

translations.literal: " When Xin was defeated, Souzhi lived on South Mountain; Luoyang inspector Wang Yuangui summoned him as central aide.
translations.idiomatic: " After Xin was defeated, Souzhi dwelt on South Mountain; Luoyang inspector Wang Yuangui appointed him central aide.

sentences.zh: 西師忽至，尋退，遂隨西師入關。

translations.literal: Western troops suddenly arrived, then soon withdrew; he thereupon followed the western army into the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Western troops came suddenly and soon withdrew; he then followed the western army through the passes into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 周文帝以為大行臺倉曹郎中，卒。

translations.literal: Prince Wen of Zhou made him director of granaries on the Grand Mobile Staff; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen of Zhou appointed him director of granaries on the grand mobile staff; he died in that post.

sentences.zh: 贈徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given inspector of Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Xu province.

sentences.zh: 讞之，字士平，七歲便勤學，早知名。

translations.literal: Yanzhi, styled Shiping, at seven sui was already diligent in study and early won fame.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi, styled Shiping, was studying hard by age seven and was known early.

sentences.zh: 累遷司徒主簿。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to chief clerk of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief clerk in the ministry of education.

sentences.zh: 楊愔每稱嘆云：「河東士族，京官不少，唯此家兄弟，全無鄉音。

translations.literal: Yang Yin would often praise him, saying, "Among the gentry clans of Hedong there are many capital officials, but only this household's brothers have no trace of home accent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin often praised him, saying, "Hedong has many families with capital officials, but only these brothers speak without a hometown accent.

sentences.zh: 」讞之雖年少，不妄交遊，唯與隴西辛術、趙郡李繪、頓丘李構、清河崔瞻為忘年之友。

translations.literal: Though Yanzhi was still young, he did not make friends lightly; only Longxi Xin Shu, Zhao commandery Li Hui, Dunqiu Li Gou, and Qinghe Cui Zhan were his friends across the years.
translations.idiomatic: Though still young, Yanzhi did not socialize lightly; only Xin Shu of Longxi, Li Hui of Zhao commandery, Li Gou of Dunqiu, and Cui Zhan of Qinghe were his friends despite the age gap.

sentences.zh: 昭帝梓宮將還鄴，轉儀曹郎，尤悉歷代故事、儀註，喪禮皆能裁正。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao's coffin was about to return to Ye, he was transferred to gentleman of the rituals bureau; he especially knew past dynasties' precedents and ritual regulations, and could correct all mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao's coffin was to return to Ye, he was made gentleman of the rituals bureau; he knew dynastic precedent and ceremonial law especially well and could set right every mourning rite.

sentences.zh: 為永昌太守，客旅過郡，出私財供給，人間無所，預代下出，為吏人所懷。

translations.literal: As grand administrator of Yongchang, when travelers passed through the commandery he supplied them from private funds; where the district had nothing, he advanced payment on their behalf, and the clerks and people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: As grand administrator of Yongchang, he paid traveling guests from his own purse when the commandery had nothing on hand, advancing funds for them in advance, and officials and commoners alike were grateful.

sentences.zh: 齊亡仕周，卒伊川太守。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou's service and died as grand administrator of Yichuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell he served Zhou and died as grand administrator of Yichuan.

sentences.zh: 皇甫和，字長諧，安定朝那人，其先因官寓居漢中。

translations.literal: Huangfu He, styled Changxie, was a man of Chaona in Anding; his ancestors because of office had taken residence in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu He, styled Changxie, was from Chaona in Anding; his forebears had settled in Hanzhong through official postings.

sentences.zh: 祖澄，南齊秦、梁二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was inspector of Qin and Liang in Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng had been inspector of Qin and Liang under Southern Qi.

sentences.zh: 父徽，字子玄，梁安定、略陽二郡守。

translations.literal: His father Hui, styled Zixuan, was grand administrator of Anding and Lüeyang in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui, styled Zixuan, had been grand administrator of Anding and Lüeyang in Liang.

sentences.zh: 魏正始二年，隨其妻父夏侯道遷入魏，道遷別上勳書，欲以徽為元謀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi in Wei, he followed his wife's father Xiahou Daoqian in entering Wei; Daoqian separately submitted a merit roster wishing to list Hui as chief conspirator.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, second year of Zhengshi, he followed his wife's father Xiahou Daoqian into Wei service; Daoqian filed a separate merit roll naming Hui as chief plotter.

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「創謀之始，本不關預，雖貪榮賞，內愧於心。

translations.literal: Hui said, "At the beginning of the plot I had no part in it; though I covet glory and reward, inwardly I am ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "I took no part when the plot began; though I crave honor and reward, my conscience would not bear it.

sentences.zh: 」遂拒而不許。

translations.literal: " He therefore refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史羊靈祐重其敦實，表為征虜府司馬，卒。

translations.literal: Liang inspector Yang Lingyou valued his honesty and substance and memorialized him as staff officer of the campaign against barbarians; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Liang inspector Yang Lingyou respected his solid character and recommended him as staff officer on the campaign against barbarians; he died in that post.

sentences.zh: 和十一而孤，母夏侯氏，才明有禮則，親授以經書。

translations.literal: He at eleven was orphaned; his mother the Lady Xiahou was talented, clear, and observant of ritual propriety, and personally taught him the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was orphaned at eleven; his mother Lady Xiahou was talented, principled, and versed in ritual, and taught him the classics herself.

sentences.zh: 及長，深沉有雅量，尤明禮儀，宗親吉凶，多相諮訪。

translations.literal: When grown he was deep and reserved, with refined capacity, especially clear in ritual propriety; kin far and near on auspicious or inauspicious occasions mostly sought his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was grave and measured, especially skilled in ritual; relatives consulted him on happy and mournful occasions.

sentences.zh: 卒於濟陰太守。

translations.literal: He died as grand administrator of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as grand administrator of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 李構，字祖基，黎陽人。

translations.literal: Li Gou, styled Zuji, was a man of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gou, styled Zuji, was from Liyang.

sentences.zh: 祖平，魏尚書僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ping was vice director of the masters of writing in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ping had been vice director of the masters of writing under Wei.

sentences.zh: 構少以方正見稱，釋褐開府參軍，累遷譙州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Gou from youth was praised for uprightness; on leaving the robe he became staff officer of an opening office, rose repeatedly to inspector of Qiao, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was known from youth for rectitude; on first appointment he joined an opening office staff, rose to inspector of Qiao, and died there.

sentences.zh: 構從父弟庶，魏大司農諧子。

translations.literal: Gou's younger cousin by the father's line was Shu; in Wei he was son of the grand minister of agriculture Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Gou's younger cousin on the father's side was Shu, son of Wei grand minister of agriculture Xie.

sentences.zh: 方雅好學，風流規檢，甚有家風。

translations.literal: Correct and elegant, he loved learning, had refined standards of conduct, and bore a strong family style.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and fond of learning, he kept strict standards of conduct and upheld the family reputation.

sentences.zh: 稍遷臨漳令。

translations.literal: He rose gradually to magistrate of Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to magistrate of Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》出，庶與盧斐、王松年等訟其不平，並繫獄。

translations.literal: When the History of Wei appeared, Shu together with Lu Fei, Wang Songnian, and others sued over its unfairness and were all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the History of Wei was published, Shu joined Lu Fei, Wang Songnian, and others in suing over its bias and was imprisoned with them.

sentences.zh: 魏收書王慧龍自云太原人，又言王瓊不善事；

translations.literal: Wei Shou wrote that Wang Huilong called himself a man of Taiyuan, and also said Wang Qiong was poor at serving;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou wrote that Wang Huilong claimed to be from Taiyuan and also said Wang Qiong was inept in his duties;

sentences.zh: 盧同附《盧玄傳》；

translations.literal: Lu Tong was attached to the biography of Lu Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong was tucked into the biography of Lu Xuan;

sentences.zh: 李平為陳留人，云其家貧賤。

translations.literal: Li Ping was made a man of Chenliu, saying his family was poor and base.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping was called a man of Chenliu and described as coming from a poor, humble house.

sentences.zh: 故裴等致訟，語楊愔云：「魏收合誅。

translations.literal: Therefore the Pei clan and others brought the suit, saying to Yang Yin, "Wei Shou ought to be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Pei party and others brought suit, telling Yang Yin, "Wei Shou deserves execution.

sentences.zh: 」愔黨助魏收，遂白顯祖罪斐等，並髡頭，鞭二百。

translations.literal: " Yin sided with Wei Shou; they thereupon reported to Gao Yang that Fei and the others were guilty, and all were shaved and given two hundred lashes.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin took Wei Shou's side; they then denounced Fei and the rest to Gao Yang, and all were shaved and flogged two hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 庶死於臨漳獄中，庶兄岳痛之，終身不歷臨漳縣門。

translations.literal: Shu died in Linzhang prison; Shu's elder brother Yue grieved for him and to the end of his life never passed Linzhang's county gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shu died in Linzhang jail; his elder brother Yue mourned him so deeply that he never again went through Linzhang's gate while he lived.

sentences.zh: 張宴之，字熙德。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanzhi, styled Xide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanzhi, styled Xide.

sentences.zh: 幼孤有至性，為母鄭氏教誨，動依禮典。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he had utmost nature; his mother the Lady Zheng taught and admonished him, and in action he always followed the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was deeply dutiful; his mother Lady Zheng raised him by the rites, and he followed them in everything.

sentences.zh: 從尒朱榮平元顥，賜爵武成子，累遷尚書二千石郎中。

translations.literal: He followed Erzhu Rong in pacifying Yuan Hao, was given the enfeoffment Baron of Wucheng, and rose repeatedly to gentleman of the two-thousand-dan rank in the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Rong in defeating Yuan Hao, was enfeoffed baron of Wucheng, and rose to gentleman of the two-thousand-dan rank in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 高岳征潁川，復以為都督中兵參軍兼記室。

translations.literal: When Gao Yue campaigned in Yingchuan, he again made Yanzhi commanding aide of central troops with concurrent recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yue campaigned in Yingchuan, he again appointed Yanzhi commanding aide of central troops with concurrent recorder.

sentences.zh: 宴之文士，兼有武幹，每與岳帷帳之謀，又常以短兵接刃，親獲首級，深為岳所嗟賞。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was a man of letters who also had martial ability; he often joined Yue in planning within the curtains, and also often took short weapons to clash at close quarters, personally taking heads—deeply admired by Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was a literatus with martial skill; he often joined Yue's council in the tent and just as often fought hand to hand with a short blade, taking heads himself—much to Yue's admiration.

sentences.zh: 天保初，文宣為高陽王納宴之女為妃，令赴晉陽成禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Gao Yang as Prince of Gaoyang took Yanzhi's daughter as consort and ordered Yanzhi to go to Jinyang to complete the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao, Gao Yang as Prince of Gaoyang married Yanzhi's daughter and ordered him to Jinyang to finish the wedding.

sentences.zh: 宴之後園陪宴，坐客皆賦詩。

translations.literal: Afterward in the rear garden he attended a feast; seated guests all composed poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a feast in the rear garden, every guest was asked to compose a poem.

sentences.zh: 宴之詩云：「天下有道，主明臣直，雖休勿休，永貽世則。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's poem said, "When the realm has the Way, the lord is bright and ministers upright; though there is rest, do not rest—forever leave a model to the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi's poem ran, "When the Way holds the realm, the ruler is bright and his ministers straight; though all is calm, do not grow calm—leave the age a lasting model.

sentences.zh: 」文宣笑曰：「得卿箴諷，深以慰懷。

translations.literal: " Gao Yang laughed and said, "To gain your admonition in verse deeply comforts my heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Yang laughed and said, "Your verse of counsel comforts me deeply.

sentences.zh: 」後行北徐州事，尋卽真，為吏人所愛。

translations.literal: " Later he acted for North Xu province and soon received the full appointment; officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: " He later administered North Xu province, soon received the regular appointment, and was beloved by officials and people.

sentences.zh: 御史崔子武督察州郡，至北徐州，無所案劾，唯得百姓所制《清德頌》數篇。

translations.literal: Censor Cui Ziwu inspected the provinces and commanderies; reaching North Xu he found nothing to impeach, only several pieces of "Pure Virtue Praise" composed by the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cui Ziwu inspected provinces and commanderies; at North Xu he found no charges to bring, only several "Hymns of Pure Virtue" written by the people.

sentences.zh: 乃歎曰：「本求罪狀，遂聞頌聲。

translations.literal: He thereupon sighed and said, "I came seeking crimes and instead heard songs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "I came looking for offenses and instead heard praise.

sentences.zh: 」遷兗州刺史，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to inspector of Yan province; before he could take up the post he died.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to inspector of Yan but died before assuming the post.

sentences.zh: 贈齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given inspector of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 陸卬，字雲駒。

translations.literal: Lu Ang, styled Yunju.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ang, styled Yunju.

sentences.zh: 少機悟，美風神，好學不倦，博覽群書，五經多通大義。

translations.literal: From youth he was quick and perceptive, of fine spirit and bearing; he loved learning without tiring, broadly reading many books, and mostly penetrated the great meaning of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quick and perceptive, handsome in spirit and bearing; he studied tirelessly, read widely, and grasped the main sense of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，甚為河間邢卲所賞。

translations.literal: Skilled at composing literature, he was greatly prized by Xing Shao of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in writing, he was greatly admired by Xing Shao of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 卲又與卬父子彰交遊，嘗謂子彰曰：「吾以卿老蚌，遂出明珠，意欲為羣拜紀可乎？

translations.literal: Shao also associated with Ang and his son Zhang in friendship. He once said to Zih Zhang, "I take you as the old clam that bore the pearl—do you wish the assembly all to bow to Ji Ke?
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao also befriended Lu Ang and his son Zhang. Once he said to Zhang, "I call you the old clam that bore the pearl—do you want everyone to bow to Ji Ke?

sentences.zh: 」由是名譽日高，儒雅搢紳，尤所推許。

translations.literal: " Thereupon his reputation rose daily; the refined scholar-gentry especially praised and upheld him.
translations.idiomatic: " From this his reputation rose day by day; cultivated officials especially praised him.

sentences.zh: 起家員外散騎侍郎，歷文襄大將軍主簿，中書舍人，兼中書侍郎，以本職兼太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He began his career as Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; he served as secretary to Gao Cheng, Grand General; Secretariat Gentleman; concurrently Secretariat Vice Director; and in his regular post concurrently Crown Prince Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He began as outer attendant of the scattered cavalry, then served as secretary to Grand General Gao Cheng, as secretariat gentleman and concurrent secretariat vice director, and in that post also as crown prince preceptor.

sentences.zh: 自梁、魏通和，歲有交聘，卬每兼官燕接。

translations.literal: From the time Liang and Wei made peace, each year brought mutual embassies; Ang each time held a concurrent post for banquet reception.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liang and Wei were at peace, embassies were exchanged every year; Ang repeatedly held concurrent posts to host the banquets.

sentences.zh: 在帝席賦詩，卬必先成，雖未能盡工，以敏速見美。

translations.literal: At imperial banquets when composing verse, Ang always finished first; though his work was not fully polished, he was admired for quickness.
translations.idiomatic: At imperial feasts when poems were set, Ang always finished first; though not always masterly, he was praised for his speed.

sentences.zh: 除中書侍郎，修國史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Vice Director and edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was made secretariat vice director and edited the national history.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，居喪盡禮，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: On his father's death he left office; in mourning he fulfilled every rite, his grief wasting him to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his father's mourning and observed every rite until grief had wasted him to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 詔以本官起。

translations.literal: An edict recalled him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him to his former post.

sentences.zh: 文襄時鎮鄴，嘉其至行，親詣門以慰勉之。

translations.literal: When Gao Cheng held Ye, he prized Ang's utmost conduct and came in person to his gate to console and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: While Gao Cheng was stationed at Ye he admired Ang's conduct, came to his door in person, and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 卬母魏上庸公主，初封藍田，高明婦人也，甚有志操。

translations.literal: Ang's mother was the Wei Princess of Shangyong, first enfeoffed as Princess of Lantian—a woman of high principle and very strong resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's mother was the Wei princess of Shangyong, first enfeoffed as princess of Lantian—a woman of high principle and strong moral resolve.

sentences.zh: 卬昆季六人，並主所生。

translations.literal: Ang had six brothers, all born of the mistress.
translations.idiomatic: Ang and six brothers were all children of the same mother.

sentences.zh: 故邢卲常謂人云：「藍田生玉，固不虛矣。

translations.literal: Thus Xing Shao often told people, "Lantian breeds jade—indeed it is no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao often said, "Lantian breeds jade—the saying is no empty boast.

sentences.zh: 」主教訓諸子，皆稟義方，雖創巨痛深，出於天性，然動依禮度，亦母氏之訓焉。

translations.literal: " The mistress instructed her sons; all received righteous training. Though their crushing grief sprang from inborn nature, in action they still followed ritual measure—also their mother's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " Their mother trained them in the right way; though their overwhelming grief came from nature, they still acted by ritual—her teaching as well.

sentences.zh: 卬兄弟相率廬於墓側，負土成墳，朝廷深所嗟尚，發詔褒揚，改其所居裏為孝終里。

translations.literal: Ang and his brothers together led huts by the tomb, carried earth to form the mound; the court deeply admired this, issued an edict of praise, and renamed their lane Xiaozhong Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Ang and his brothers built mourning huts beside the tomb and heaped the grave with their own hands; the court admired them deeply, issued a commendation, and renamed their lane Xiaozhong, "Filial End."

sentences.zh: 服竟當襲，不忍嗣侯。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was due to inherit, but he could not bear to succeed to the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was to inherit the title, but he could not bring himself to take the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 天保初，常山王薦卬器幹，文宣面授給事黃門侍郎，遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao, the Prince of Changshan recommended Ang's talent and capacity; Gao Yang personally appointed him Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate Attendant, then promoted him to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao the prince of Changshan recommended Ang's ability; Gao Yang personally appointed him supervising secretary of the yellow gate attendant, then made him director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 上洛王思宗為清都尹，辟為邑中正，食貝丘縣幹。

translations.literal: Prince of Shangluo Sizong was magistrate of Qingdu; he summoned Ang as director of the district selection office and granted him the salary of Beiqiu county.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Shangluo Sizong was magistrate of Qingdu he appointed Ang head of the local selection office with the salary of Beiqiu county.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，哀慕毀悴，殆不勝喪，至沉篤，頓昧伏枕。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he mourned with such grief and wasting that he nearly could not survive the mourning; he fell critically ill, collapsed in a stupor, and lay on his pillow.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's death he grieved until he was near broken by mourning; he grew critically ill, collapsed in a stupor, and could not rise from his pillow.

sentences.zh: 又感風疾。

translations.literal: He also contracted a wind ailment.
translations.idiomatic: He also contracted a wind disorder.

sentences.zh: 第五弟摶遇疾臨終，謂其兄弟曰：「大兄尫病如此，性至慈愛，摶之死日，必不得使大兄知之，哭泣聲必不可聞徹，致有感慟。

translations.literal: His fifth younger brother Tuan, facing illness at life's end, told his brothers, "Our eldest brother's wasting illness is like this, and his nature is deeply loving. On the day of Tuan's death you must not let the eldest brother know; sounds of weeping must not be heard reaching through, lest it stir his grief.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth brother Tuan, on his deathbed, told the others, "The eldest brother is this ill and tender-hearted. On the day I die you must not let him know; no weeping must reach him, or it will break his heart.

sentences.zh: 」家人至於祖載，方始告之。

translations.literal: " The family only told him when the funeral procession set out.
translations.idiomatic: " The family told him only when the funeral cortege departed.

sentences.zh: 卬聞而悲痛，一慟便絕，年四十八。

translations.literal: Ang heard and grieved; one great sob and he died—forty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Ang heard, he grieved; one great sob and he was gone, at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 卬自在朝，篤慎固密，不說人短，不伐己長，言論清遠，有人倫鑒裁，朝野甚悲惜之。

translations.literal: Ang in court was earnest, cautious, and tight-lipped; he spoke no man's faults and boasted no merit of his own. His discourse was clear and far-reaching; he had discernment in human relations. Court and countryside deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: In office Ang was earnest and discreet; he spoke ill of no one and boasted of nothing. His speech was clear and measured, and he judged men well. Court and country mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈衛將軍、青州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General of the Guards and inspector of Qing province; his posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general of the guards and inspector of Qing province, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 所著文章十四卷，行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings in fourteen scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writings in fourteen scrolls circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 齊之效廟諸歌，多卬所制。

translations.literal: Many of the Qi suburban-temple songs were composed by Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the Qi suburban-temple hymns were Ang's work.

sentences.zh: 子乂嗣，襲爵始平侯。

translations.literal: His son Yi succeeded and inherited the marquisate of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi succeeded to the marquisate of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 王松年，少知名。

translations.literal: Wang Songnian was known from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Songnian was known from his youth.

sentences.zh: 文襄臨幷州，辟為主簿，累遷通直散騎常侍，副李緯使梁。

translations.literal: When Gao Cheng took Bingzhou he summoned him as secretary; he rose through posts to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and served as deputy to Li Wei on an embassy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng took Bingzhou he made Songnian his secretary; he rose to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and went to Liang as deputy to Li Wei.

sentences.zh: 還，歷位尚書郎中。

translations.literal: On his return he held successive posts as director in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he served in successive director posts in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 魏收撰《魏書》成，松年有謗言，文宣怒，禁止之，仍加杖罰。

translations.literal: When Wei Shou finished compiling the Book of Wei, Songnian spoke slanderously of it; Gao Yang was angry, had him detained, and also had him beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Shou completed the Book of Wei, Songnian spoke against it; Gao Yang was furious, had him imprisoned, and had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 歲餘得免，除臨漳令，遷司馬、別駕、本州大中正。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was released, appointed magistrate of Linzhang, then promoted to aide, chief administrator, and grand selection officer of his province.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was freed, made magistrate of Linzhang, then promoted to aide, chief administrator, and provincial grand selection officer.

sentences.zh: 孝昭擢拜給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Gao Yan promoted him to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan promoted him to supervising secretary of the yellow gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝每賜坐，與論政事，甚善之。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor granted him a seat and discussed state affairs with him, he was well pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor gave him a seat and discussed affairs, he favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 孝昭崩，松年馳驛至鄴都宣遺詔，發言涕泗，迄於宣罷，容色無改，辭吐諧韻。

translations.literal: When Gao Yan died, Songnian galloped by post relay to Ye to proclaim the testament; as he spoke, tears streamed down, yet from the start of the proclamation to its end his bearing did not change and his words kept their rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan died, Songnian raced by post to Ye to proclaim the deathbed edict; he wept as he spoke, yet from beginning to end his composure did not alter and his delivery stayed measured.

sentences.zh: 宣訖，號慟自絕於地，百官莫不感慟。

translations.literal: When the proclamation ended he wailed and threw himself to the ground; the hundred officials were all deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading ended he collapsed wailing; every official was moved.

sentences.zh: 還晉陽，兼侍中，護梓宮還鄴。

translations.literal: He returned to Jinyang, concurrently Palace Attendant, and escorted the coffin back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Jinyang as concurrent palace attendant and escorted the coffin to Ye.

sentences.zh: 諸舊臣避形跡，無敢盡哀，唯松年哭甚流涕，朝士咸恐。

translations.literal: The old ministers restrained their bearing; none dared show full grief—only Songnian wept with streaming tears, and the courtiers were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Former ministers held themselves in check and none dared mourn openly; only Songnian wept freely, and courtiers were uneasy.

sentences.zh: 武成雖忿松年戀舊情切，亦雅重之。

translations.literal: Though Gao Zhan resented Songnian's deep attachment to the old reign, he also held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Though Gao Zhan resented Songnian's loyalty to the late emperor, he still respected him.

sentences.zh: 以本官加散騎常侍，食高邑縣幹，參定律令，前後大事多委焉。

translations.literal: In his regular post he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, granted the salary of Gaoyi county, and took part in compiling laws and statutes; major affairs before and after were largely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry with the salary of Gaoyi county, helped compile laws and statutes, and was entrusted with one major affair after another.

sentences.zh: 兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 發晉陽之鄴，在道遇疾卒。

translations.literal: Setting out from Jinyang for Ye, he fell ill on the road and died.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Jinyang for Ye, he fell ill on the road and died.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書、幷州刺史，諡曰平。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Personnel and inspector of Bing province; his posthumous title was Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of personnel and inspector of Bing province, with the posthumous name Ping.

sentences.zh: 第三子卲，最知名。

translations.literal: The third son Shao was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: The third son, Xing Shao, was the most famous.

sentences.zh: 劉禕，字彥英，彭城人。

translations.literal: Liu Yi, style Yanying, was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, style Yanying, was from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 父世明，魏兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Shiming had been Wei inspector of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shiming had been Wei inspector of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 禕性弘裕，有威重，容止可觀，雖昵友密交，朝夕遊處，莫不加敬。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was broad and generous; he had weight and dignity; his bearing was admirable. Though intimate friends kept close company day and night, none failed to treat him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was magnanimous and dignified, with a bearing men admired; even close friends who spent every day with him treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 好學，善《三禮》，吉凶儀制，尤所留心。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled in the Three Rites; rites of fortune and calamity especially held his attention.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and excelled in the Three Rites, especially the ceremonies of fortune and mourning.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌中，釋巾太學博士。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei he doffed his headcloth and became Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wei Xiaochang era he entered the academy as erudite.

sentences.zh: 累遷睢州刺史，邊人服其威信，甚得疆埸之和。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to inspector of Sui province; the frontier people submitted to his prestige and trust, and the borderlands knew great peace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to inspector of Sui province; frontier people trusted his authority and the border was at peace.

sentences.zh: 世宗輔政，降書褒獎，云：「以卿家世忠純，奕代冠冕，賢弟賢子，並與吾共事，懷抱相托，亦自依然。

translations.literal: When Gao Cheng held the regency he sent a letter of commendation, saying, "With your family's generations of loyal purity and successive generations in caps and coronets, worthy younger brothers and worthy sons all serve with me—hearts entrusted to one another, still as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng was regent he sent a letter of praise, saying, "Your house has been loyal for generations and worn court rank for ages; worthy brothers and sons serve at my side, and the trust between us is unchanged.

sentences.zh: 宜勗心力，以副所委，莫慮不富貴。

translations.literal: You should exert your mind and strength to answer what is entrusted—do not worry that wealth and rank will not come.
translations.idiomatic: Exert yourself to fulfill what I entrust to you; do not doubt that honor and wealth will follow.

sentences.zh: 」秩滿，逕歸鄉里侍父疾，竟不入朝。

translations.literal: " When his term ended he went straight home to nurse his father's illness and never entered court.
translations.idiomatic: " When his term ended he went home to tend his father's illness and never returned to court.

sentences.zh: 父喪，沉頓累年，非杖不起。

translations.literal: On his father's death he was prostrate for years and could not rise without a staff.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he lay prostrate for years and could not rise without a staff.

sentences.zh: 世宗致辟，禕稱疾不動。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng summoned him, but Yi pleaded illness and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng summoned him, but Yi pleaded illness and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 五子，璇、玘、璞、瑗、瓚，並有志節，為世所稱。

translations.literal: Five sons—Xuan, Qi, Pu, Yuan, and Zan—all had resolve and principle and were praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Five sons—Xuan, Qi, Pu, Yuan, and Zan—all had moral resolve and were praised in their time.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
